home.title: Preserving and Celebrating Cooperative Cultural Heritage – Sites, Traditions and Practices that connect communities around the world across generations.

whatIs.title: What is Cooperative Cultural Heritage?
whatIs.desc: Cooperative Cultural Heritage (CCH) refers to the tangible and intangible heritage that is created, maintained, and transmitted by cooperative organizations. It includes a wide range of cultural expressions, from the architectural design of cooperative buildings to the songs, stories, and traditions that are passed down through generations of cooperative members. CCH is a living heritage that is constantly evolving, and it plays an important role in shaping the identity of cooperative communities around the world.

tangible.title: Tangible Heritage of Cooperation
tangible.desc: Tangible heritage includes the physical artifacts and sites that are associated with the history of the cooperative movement. This can include everything from the first cooperative store to the modern-day headquarters of a cooperative federation. These sites and artifacts provide a tangible link to the past and help to preserve the memory of the cooperative movement for future generations.

intangible.title: Intangible Heritage of Cooperation
intangible.desc: Intangible heritage includes the traditions, practices, and expressions of culture that are passed down through generations of cooperative members. This can include everything from the songs and stories that are told about the cooperative movement to the unique governance structures and decision-making processes that are used by cooperatives. Intangible heritage is a living heritage that is constantly evolving, and it plays an important role in shaping the identity of cooperative communities around the world.

principles.title: Principles for Identifying Cooperative Cultural Heritage
principles.desc: The criteria and the first (2025) standards employed in identifying the Cooperative Cultural Heritage.

modal.title: Principles for Identifying Cooperative Cultural Heritage
modal.text: A thirteen point set of international standards on Cooperative Cultural Heritage was drawn up by the ICA Working Group on CCH in fall 2025. These standards, the first of its kind, will build on experiences through 2026, by which time, the ICA aims to list at least 50 CCH sites and 15 CCH intangible elements (through a separate set of criterions) from across all the regions, representing all ICA sectors, selected through a nomination process, open to the members of the ICA and their constituents. A unique ICA-CCH label will be granted to the selected sites that meet all the 13 criterions along with a Statement of Recognition, in a post launch (November 2025) exercise.

charter.title: Charter on the Recognition of Cooperative Cultural Heritage Sites

preamble.title: Preamble
preamble.p1: Recognizing that cooperatives are not only enterprises but also bearers of culture, history, and identity, this Charter establishes a framework for the recognition and safeguarding of cooperative cultural heritage sites.
preamble.p2: These criteria aim to ensure that cooperative heritage is preserved, celebrated, and integrated into wider cultural narratives while continuing to inspire present and future generations in line with the values of democracy, equity, solidarity, and sustainability.
preamble.p3: This Charter affirms the commitment of the cooperative movement to recognize, preserve, and promote its cultural heritage. By adopting these criteria, cooperative heritage sites shall become living symbols of solidarity, education, and international cooperation.
